name: Vitya and Strange Lesson
description: Today at the lesson Vitya learned a very interesting function — mex . Mex of a sequence of numbers is the minimum non-negative number that is not present in the sequence as element. For example, mex ([4, 33, 0, 1, 1, 5]) = 2 and mex ([1, 2, 3]) = 0 . Vitya quickly understood all tasks of the teacher, but can you do the same? You are given an array consisting of n non-negative integers, and m queries. Each query is characterized by one number x and consists of the following consecutive steps: Perform the bitwise addition operation modulo 2 ( xor ) of each array element with the number x . Find mex of the resulting array. Note that after each query the array changes.
input_specification: First line contains two integer numbers n and m ( 1 ≤ n , m ≤ 3·10 5 ) — number of elements in array and number of queries. Next line contains n integer numbers a i ( 0 ≤ a i ≤ 3·10 5 ) — elements of then array. Each of next m lines contains query — one integer number x ( 0 ≤ x ≤ 3·10 5 ).
output_specification: For each query print the answer on a separate line.
approach_summary: Maintain prefix sums and dynamic point updates via Fenwick tree using lowbit operations (i & -i) in O(log N) time and O(N) space.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 842D — Vitya and Strange Lesson [70. BIT / Fenwick Tree]
topic_editorial.summary: Point updates and range prefix queries with Fenwick Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every integer $i$ has a unique binary decomposition. Index $i$ in a Binary Indexed Tree stores the cumulative sum of the interval $(i - \text{lowbit}(i), i]$, allowing logarithmic traversal via $i \mathrel{+}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$ and $i \mathrel{-}= (i \mathbin{\&} -i)$.
